hints.title: Bidirectional Consecutive Paths
hints.text: A continuous consecutive path can pass through a node by connecting an increasing branch on one side to a decreasing branch on the other.

hints.title: Two-Length Subproblem Tuple
hints.text: From each subtree, return a pair (inc_len, dec_len) representing maximum lengths of increasing and decreasing paths starting downward from node.

hints.title: Bottom-Up Path Joining
hints.text: Compare node.val with left and right children. If child.val == node.val + 1, inc = max(inc, child_inc + 1). If child.val == node.val - 1, dec = max(dec, child_dec + 1). Update global maximum with inc + dec - 1.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Single post-order traversal computing branch lengths in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Top-down path exploration re-evaluates overlapping paths in O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Returning (inc, dec) allows joining left and right consecutive slopes in O(1) time per node.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use post-order traversal returning (increasing, decreasing) lengths.
